title: You pointed at them.
paragraphs:
You pointed at them.
But heaven was pointing at you.
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable.

You felt it—
that quiet satisfaction…
that subtle “I’m better than this.”
And now there’s a question hanging in the air:

What if the thing you hate in them…
is the thing you refuse to face in yourself?
Because Jesus didn’t say this to the worst sinners.
He said it to the religious ones.

The careful ones.
The disciplined ones.
The “I would never do that” crowd.
And then He dropped a blade:
“Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but do not notice the plank that is in your own eye?” — Matthew 7:3
Here’s the truth we don’t like to admit:
Pride is the most invisible sin to the one who carries it.

You can spot lust in others.
You can call out compromise.
You can analyze behavior like a judge in a courtroom.

It hides behind “discernment.”
It disguises itself as “righteous anger.”
It whispers, “You’re just being honest.”
You don’t just see their sin.
Build quiet cases in your mind.
He said deal with yours first.
“First take the plank out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother’s eye.” — Matthew 7:5

Because we want to fix others
before we surrender ourselves.
But God doesn’t work that way.
Let me say something that might shake you:

You can be right about their sin…
and still be wrong before God.
Because God is not just looking at what you see.
He’s looking at how you see.
The Pharisees were experts in pointing out sin.
“This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.” — Matthew 15:8
that’s where you are right now.

But when was the last time
you let those same Scriptures break you?
Because this isn’t just about behavior.
“The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it?” — Jeremiah 17:9
Because the same Jesus who exposed the plank…
…is the same Jesus who carried your cross.
While you were busy analyzing others—
He was fully aware of everything in you.

Every hidden motive.
Every quiet arrogance.
Every secret thought.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Not after you removed the plank.
Because when you truly see the cross—
You lose the right to look down on anyone.
At the foot of the cross:

The liar and the leader stand equal.
The addict and the achiever kneel the same.
The broken and the “put together” are both desperate for mercy.
That’s what real transformation looks like.
So here’s the question you can’t avoid anymore:
What plank have you been protecting?
That hidden sin you’ve renamed as “personality”?
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
You don’t have to keep carrying what Jesus already died to remove.
And if this pierced something deep—
